request.description:
The stream path of `ticfac watch` (piped stdout or --json) spells the attempt-hold settle command inline as `ticfac settle <epic> <tick> <attempt> --release "<who>"` with no --run-id. For a cloud run the attempt lives in the run_<hex> store the bare command's default (epic-<epic>) never opens, so the command the alert names refuses; a local run watched under a non-epic-shaped id (the pipeline fixture's own run-p) breaks the same way. The model path spells it right via SettleCommandForCurrent; this branch formats the command inline. This tick fixed only the triage branch of the same alert — this tick's seam; the settle branch is the same shape one verb over and deserves its own test against a cloud or non-epic run id.
evidence: internal/cli/watch.go:366-373 (inline settle format); compare statusmodel.SettleCommandForCurrent; reproduces for any run id that is not epic-<epic>, e.g. the pipeline fixture's run-p

ticfac run run_f44b6ad8909b495cbd3bae4ee7cf229c created this tick by absorbing the finding ccf368ecc7bc53fe8b78248de4bab07e1415dc811d5b29990050e890080edc9b (reported by run-run_f44b6ad8909b495cbd3bae4ee7cf229c/tick-q8m/attempt-1): the finding was judged against the epic's definition of done and gates done item A2. The decision record — item id, verdict, observed or predicted, confidence — is .ticfac/runs/run_f44b6ad8909b495cbd3bae4ee7cf229c/absorptions/ccf368ecc7bc53fe8b78248de4bab07e1415dc811d5b29990050e890080edc9b.json on the run branch.
request.title: Watch's stream-path settle alert names no --run-id for a non-default run id
